solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gruff and grumpy about European no doubt

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: surly means both gruff and grumpy
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sour-tempered continental, adding that there is no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two adjectives together give a single word; the E sits after the first three letters of SURLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb of certainty, used just like the phrase meaning without any question.

clue.text: Is English sailor of Royal Navy “marine”?

blocks.note: 's is the contracted form of is, as in it's
E is the abbreviation for English
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard crossword sailor
o' is the clipped form of of, as in o'clock
RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A question about whether an English sailor in the Royal Navy counts as a marine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and quotation marks invite a debate about service branches; 'Is' is only the contraction 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something born of the ocean is marine in origin, so the poetic compound adjective matches.

clue.text: French one to drag round aged trotters

indicators.note: turning something round sends it back the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: un is French for one
to lug is to drag something heavy
ae. (aetatis) is the abbreviation for aged, as on gravestones

explanation.surface: A Frenchman hauls an old pair of pig's feet around.
explanation.walkthrough: AE, short for the Latin aetatis, is how gravestones and dictionaries abbreviate aged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungulae is the Latin-derived plural for hoofs, and trotters are animal feet ending in hoofs.

clue.text: With a weighty wallet freshly adorned, my eye!

indicators.note: something done freshly is made anew, so these letters are set out again in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An incredulous retort that a rich person has just been prettied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My eye!' reads as an exclamation of disbelief, but those five letters are part of the material being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well supplied with cash in hand means carrying a fat purse, the sense of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Splenetic press note a term for immoral

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter of the next word is wanted

blocks.note: to lie on something is to press down on it
N is the abbreviation for note
taken as written
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered newspaper item brands someone's conduct as immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splenetic' looks like ill temper but is used in its literal sense of the spleen; 'term' means end, as in terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives meaning pertaining to the spleen, the organ whose Latin name is lien.

clue.text: Oddly wet inside upcoming ghostly aspect of God’s acre?

indicators.note: something done oddly is done strangely, so these letters come out in an unusual order
in a down clue coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
being inside means being enclosed, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: eery is a variant spelling of eerie, meaning ghostly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spooky description of a damp churchyard seen from below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a take-every-other-letter instruction, but WT gives nothing usable; it rearranges the whole of WET. God's acre is an old name for a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are the evergreen trees traditionally planted in English churchyards, so one is a typical feature there.

clue.text: Place behind obscure English whisky

indicators.note: to be behind is to come after, so the first-named piece is placed second

blocks.note: to obscure or something obscure: dim
PL is the abbreviation for place
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a bottle of English spirit away out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like the definition, a spot to hide something, but it is an abbreviation; Dimple is a long-established brand of blended Scotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimple is the trade name of a Haig blended Scotch sold in a pinched bottle, so it is a whisky.

clue.text: “Two-rayed”, adjective in Shorter Oxford, say

indicators.note: making a word shorter means trimming letters off its end
to be in something is to be held within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a. is the dictionary abbreviation for adjective
the Oxford is an example of a dictionary, here clipped to its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry quoting a technical word and its part of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorter Oxford' looks like the title of the famous dictionary, but 'Shorter' is the cutting instruction and 'say' marks Oxford as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Diact describes a sponge spicule having two rays, the zoological term for a two-pointed structure.

clue.text: Sudden arrival sadly ruins hospital

indicators.note: things that turn out sadly have gone wrong, so the letters end up disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An unexpected influx of patients wrecks a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it is just letters to rearrange along with the hospital abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a rapid flowing in, a synonym for an influx or abrupt coming.

clue.text: Who’d write sagas? TV’s traveller, driver of dim manner

blocks.note: Michael Palin, the television travel presenter
DR is the abbreviation for driver
o' is the clipped form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
a mist makes things dim, the hazy state described

explanation.surface: Wondering which author pens epic tales, perhaps a TV presenter who travels by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sagas' suggests Norse epics, but the word reads the same backwards, which is the real point of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A palindromist composes words or phrases that read identically in both directions, and sagas is one such word.

clue.text: Fix up grand Chinese tin

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Instructions to repair a large Chinese metal container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' looks like the metal but is slang for money; the liang was a Chinese unit of weight used as currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The liang, or tael, was a Chinese weight of silver serving as money, and tin is old slang for cash.

clue.text: End of one, however poetically, with small moral significance

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
tho' is the poetic clipped form of though, meaning however
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a poem ends with little in the way of moral point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with small' reads as describing the significance, but small just supplies a single abbreviation letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic moral spirit of a person or work, its ethical import or value.

clue.text: Lurk as new militia, with leader ousted, reassembles

indicators.note: the leader is the first in line, and ousting it drops the opening letter
putting things together again differently rearranges the letters into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebel force regroups after its commander is deposed, and hides in ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the militia, but it is part of the material being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to stay concealed ready to ambush, which is just what lurking means.

clue.text: Clued up about Channel pottery

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: being clued up means being well informed
in metal casting a gate is the channel through which molten metal enters the mould

explanation.surface: Someone well informed about the ceramics of the Channel Islands or coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes 'Channel' look like the English Channel; it is a technical sense of a narrow passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Agateware is earthenware streaked to look like the mineral agate, so it is a type of pottery.

clue.text: Something immature on the way of the warrior

blocks.note: a bud is a flower not yet opened
o' is a clipped form of on, as in o' nights

explanation.surface: A beginner sets out on the warrior's path.
explanation.walkthrough: Budo is the collective Japanese name for the martial arts, literally the warrior's way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese term combines bu, military, and do, path, so it literally translates the warrior's way.

clue.text: Raincoat leads to mild irritation to back

indicators.note: leads are what go in front, so only the opening letters are kept
going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
to and on are interchangeable, as when a door is pushed to or a light put on

explanation.surface: A wet-weather coat causes a little chafing across the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the part of the body the coat rubs; it reverses the small word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mino is a traditional Japanese cape woven from straw or rushes and worn against the rain.

clue.text: What happen in glee clubs? Breaks to take in Dynasty

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to break something is to part it
the Song were a Chinese ruling dynasty

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about choir rehearsals, with interludes spent watching the TV soap Dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D and 'glee clubs' suggest the 1980s soap; it is the Chinese ruling house. Glee clubs are choral societies.
explanation.definitionFit: Part songs are pieces for several voices in harmony, the staple repertoire of a choral glee club.

clue.text: Pun about length of a branch

blocks.note: in an old dialect sense to pun is to pound or ram down
a is an abbreviation for about
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A joke about how long a bough is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pun' looks like wordplay humour, but here it is an obsolete verb for pounding; 'about' is a letter, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramal comes from Latin ramus, a bough, and describes anything pertaining to tree branches.

clue.text: Australian beast is chained up

indicators.note: when things are up they are in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild creature from Australia has been tethered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chained up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'up' is the rearranging signal acting on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal native to Australia, a classic animal of that continent.

clue.text: A cast’s blooming acting for ice cream

indicators.note: something blooming is opening out and changing shape, so the letters unfold in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a military rank

explanation.surface: A theatre company's flourishing performance earns them a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' reads as mild slang praise for the acting; it rearranges the letters, while 'acting' adds a single abbreviation letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian dessert of layered ice cream containing candied fruit and nuts.

clue.text: Candidate’s not out to proceed secretly on east

blocks.note: n.o. is how a cricket scorecard marks a batter not out
to mine is to tunnel, advancing unseen
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A political hopeful is not quitting the race but plots quietly in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out' is the cricket term for a batter still in, abbreviated on scorecards; 'on' places the last letter after.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for office or an award, which is what a candidate is.

clue.text: Wholly discharge all but final urges

indicators.note: keeping all but the final means the closing letter is dropped

blocks.note: all can mean wholly, as in all alone
to egest is to discharge from the body

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty everything except the last of one's impulses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urges' looks like a noun for desires, but it is the verb, as in putting forward an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or put forward a claim, the older sense in which one urges a point.

clue.text: Heart of those in rich Aegean region that’s luxuriant

indicators.note: the heart is the very centre, so only the middle letter is kept
something rich is elaborate and worked over, so the letters are reworked
to be in something is to be enclosed, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: the central letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lush, fertile part of the Greek islands described in travel-brochure terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aegean' places the scene in Greece, but the answer is a zoological region of the Americas; 'that's luxuriant' is descriptive colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Neogaea is the biogeographical name for the Neotropical realm of Central and South America, a faunal region.

clue.text: Aged Australian dandy raised to be unreal

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: ae. (aetatis) is the abbreviation for aged
in Australian slang a lair is a flashily dressed show-off

explanation.surface: An elderly Australian fop is lifted into some ethereal state.
explanation.walkthrough: A lair is Australian slang for a vulgarly dressed young man, a flashy dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerial can mean airy and insubstantial, imaginary like a castle in the air, hence lacking reality.

clue.text: Short paragraph by old lecturer is spoken

indicators.note: something short has been cut down, so the word is clipped to its abbreviated form

blocks.note: the word cut down to its first three letters
O is the abbreviation for old
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A brief passage from a former teacher is read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply strings the pieces together; the legal term is less familiar than its paroled cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: In law parol means given by word of mouth rather than in writing, an oral term.

clue.text: Person closing occasion with no husband is perhaps a butler

indicators.note: with no husband means the husband abbreviation is removed
closing round something shuts it in, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: per. is the grammatical abbreviation for person
an hour is a particular time or occasion

explanation.surface: Someone wrapping up a party without the man of the house turns out to be the household servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person closing' suggests whoever ends the event; Person shrinks to an abbreviation that surrounds the shortened occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler serves wine at table, so he is one example of somebody who dispenses drinks.

clue.text: Edward was one caught playing with gold on heraldic form

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a play that is on is being performed
a fess is a broad horizontal band across a heraldic shield
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A medieval king was arrested while toying with treasure on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold on heraldic form' puts the gold piece after the band, as in an across answer one thing sits on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was the eleventh-century English king given that title for his piety.

clue.text: Rodent is evasive fully raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: coy means shy and evasive
up can mean completely, as in eat up

explanation.surface: A shy creature rises fully onto its hind legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fully raised' reads as standing up straight; it is a short word for completely, turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria, farmed for its fur.

clue.text: Close to one feasible flaming rocket

blocks.note: on can mean near, as in a town on the coast
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means feasible or acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: A firework launch that comes close to working.
explanation.walkthrough: A flaming onion was a First World War anti-aircraft projectile, a string of fireballs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word named a burning anti-aircraft missile in the First World War, so it fits a fiery projectile.

clue.text: Fresh mug taking the place of everything in servery

indicators.text: taking the place of everything in
indicators.note: taking the place of everything inside means swapping out all the interior letters while keeping the ends

blocks.note: a scullery is a back kitchen where food is served and washed up
a mug is a fool, as is an ass

explanation.surface: A clean cup replaces every item in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the mug but is the definition, in its sense of cheeky; only the first and last letters of the room survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of impudent or forward is a synonym of sassy, meaning cheeky and bold.

clue.text: No good type with no hope gets a heavy blow

indicators.note: with no good, the abbreviation for good is taken away

blocks.note: a goner is someone beyond hope

explanation.surface: A worthless, hopeless character takes a hard punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' reads as describing the type, but it removes G from the start of the hopeless case.
explanation.definitionFit: Oner is British slang for a single knockout punch, one thump that finishes the job.

clue.text: French kept woman about, tad short of time

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a is an abbreviation for about
a mite is a tiny amount, a tad
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Parisian mistress hangs around, just a little pressed for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives a single letter here rather than wrapping anything; the T for time is what comes out of the tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: In French amie means a female friend and by extension a mistress or girlfriend kept by a man.

clue.text: New ad’s about one clique trapping male being conciliatory?

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a different order
to be about something is to surround it
to trap is to hold inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ring is a closed group or clique
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A fresh advertisement depicts a cliquey group hemming in a man who is trying to be pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a punning definition: taking someone's weapons away literally, or charming them into goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarming means winning over or allaying hostility, a charming conciliatory manner; literally it is also removing arms.

clue.text: Who cannot write good verse or bad operettas?

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about an incompetent writer of either poems or light operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' seems to offer a second kind of bad writer, but it only joins the definition to the material being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is an inferior rhymester, a versifier lacking talent, so it names an inept poet.

clue.text: Box with orderly — fine and right to go, more than is right

indicators.note: letters that are to go are removed from the words

blocks.note: a box can be a collecting box, a fund of money
ruly is the rare positive of unruly, meaning orderly
F is the abbreviation for fine and R for right; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: Boxing alongside a medical orderly, with a referee's ruling about what is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital attendant, but it is the adjective whose rare form ruly is the opposite of unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unduly means excessively or to an unwarranted degree, going beyond what is proper.

clue.text: Rocky edges are dotted about

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
dotted with jewels is set with them

explanation.surface: Jagged ridges are scattered here and there across the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotted about' reads as one phrase meaning scattered; it splits into a synonym and a turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An arete is a sharp, narrow mountain ridge formed by glaciers, so these are rocky crests.
